subject.title: Add loop-aware compaction guard for saturated sessions

question: Should saturated-session loop awareness live as a new agents.defaults.compaction.guard flow, be folded into the existing tools.loopDetection.postCompactionGuard and safeguard qualityGuard surfaces, or be deferred until a sanitized/live incident fixture proves the broader policy?
rationale: The remaining work adds config/default surface, runtime compaction policy, validator semantics, and reset recommendations; those choices can affect existing long-session behavior and require maintainer product intent.

options.title: Design integrated guard first
options.body: Keep this issue open while maintainers choose the permanent config and reset policy, then update or replace the partial config PR with an implementation backed by a fixture.

options.title: Use the config PR as the seed
options.body: Adopt https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/48278 as the first slice, but require explicit follow-up ownership for detector, runtime hook, validator, and reset behavior.

options.title: Defer until fixture proof
options.body: Leave the shipped post-compaction and quality guards unchanged until a current-main live or sanitized fixture demonstrates the broader saturated-session failure.

recommendation.title: Design integrated guard first
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open while maintainers choose the permanent config and reset policy, then update or replace the partial config PR with an implementation backed by a fixture.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent adjacent post-compaction guard and compaction-planning work makes this the best available owner for the config/product-shape decision.
